7
A train, initially at rest at a station, has a uniform acceleration of 0.20 m s–2 until it reaches a
speed of 20 m s–1. It travels for a time at this constant speed and then has a uniform deceleration
of 0.40 m s–2 until it comes to rest at the next station. The distance between the two stations is
3000 m.
What is the time taken by the train to travel between the two stations?
A
75 s
B
150 s
C
230 s
D
300 s

hints: Notice the motion has three parts: uniform acceleration at $0.20 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, constant speed, then uniform deceleration at $0.40 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to rest.
Use $v = u + at$ to find the accelerating time and decelerating time, and $s = (u+v)t/2$ to find the distance used in those two parts.
Subtract the accelerating and decelerating distances from 3000 m to find the middle distance at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then add all three times.
walkthrough: Find the accelerating time from rest: $t_1 = v/a_1 = 20/0.20 = 100 \text{ s}$. Distance is average velocity times time: $s_1 = (0+20)t_1/2 = 10 \times 100 = 1000 \text{ m}$.
Find the decelerating time to rest: $t_3 = v/a_3 = 20/0.40 = 50 \text{ s}$. Distance is $s_3 = (20+0)t_3/2 = 10 \times 50 = 500 \text{ m}$.
Find the middle constant-speed distance: $s_2 = 3000 - s_1 - s_3 = 3000 - 1000 - 500 = 1500 \text{ m}$.
Find the middle time at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $t_2 = s_2/v = 1500/20 = 75 \text{ s}$.
Add the three times: $t = t_1 + t_2 + t_3 = 100 + 75 + 50 = 225 \text{ s}$, which is given as option C. This is option C.

A.explanation: 75 s is only the time spent at the constant $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for the middle 1500 m, not the total accelerating plus constant-speed plus decelerating time.

B.explanation: 150 s is the sum of the accelerating time 100 s and decelerating time 50 s, omitting the 75 s travelled at constant speed.

C.explanation: Accelerating for 100 s covers 1000 m and decelerating for 50 s covers 500 m, leaving 1500 m at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for 75 s, giving total time about 225 s, represented by option C.

D.explanation: 300 s is too large and would give a velocity-time area much greater than the 3000 m station separation.
